questions.question: What is a good food cost percentage for a restaurant?
questions.answer: A good food cost percentage is 28-35% of the menu price. Fine dining can go up to 38%; fast casual should stay below 30%. MenuPricer calculates this automatically for every dish.

questions.question: How do I calculate menu pricing?
questions.answer: Divide your ingredient cost by your target food cost percentage. If a dish costs $4 to make and you want 30% food cost, the menu price is $4 / 0.30 = $13.33. MenuPricer automates this and shows Budget, Standard, and Premium price tiers.

questions.question: Do I need written recipes to use MenuPricer?
questions.answer: No. MenuPricer drafts an ingredient list and typical quantities from the dish name alone, which you then correct to match how your kitchen actually cooks. This is the difference from tools that require you to import existing recipe cards before producing any number.

questions.question: How much does DoorDash charge restaurants?
questions.answer: DoorDash charges 15-30% commission depending on plan (Basic: 25-30%, Plus: 20-25%, Premier: 15%), plus ~2.9% payment processing. MenuPricer calculates a delivery-adjusted price that offsets these fees.

questions.question: Is MenuPricer free to use?
questions.answer: Yes. MenuPricer is free for up to 5 dishes with no credit card required. The Pro plan ($9/month or $79/year) unlocks unlimited dishes, batch pricing, and PDF export.

questions.question: What currencies does MenuPricer support?
questions.answer: MenuPricer supports USD, CNY (Chinese Yuan), EUR, GBP (British Pound), CAD (Canadian Dollar), and AUD (Australian Dollar). You can switch currencies from the settings panel at the top of the page.

questions.question: How do I price a dish for delivery vs. dine-in?
questions.answer: Set your dine-in price based on food cost + target margin. Then add 15-25% for delivery platforms to offset commissions. MenuPricer shows both prices in every pricing report.
